subtype: Laughter and panic in a class [Actor]
passage:
Monday: at lunch Deepak said his cousin in 7B heard the maths test was moved to tomorrow, full syllabus. Within ten minutes the whole of 7A knew. Vikas felt his stomach flip. Girls were copying notes; one boy was nearly crying. Vikas hadn't checked anything, but his hands were already cold.
Tuesday: Mr Pillai walked in, frowned at the worried faces and said, 'The test is on Friday. Two chapters. Who told you otherwise?' Nobody could say.
Friday: the test went fine. At break, someone ran in shouting that sports day was cancelled. Vikas felt the same flip starting. He took a breath and walked to the staffroom to ask instead.

qa.q: What did Deepak say about the maths test on Monday?
qa.a: Deepak said his cousin in 7B heard the maths test was moved to tomorrow, full syllabus.

qa.q: What was Vikas feeling on Monday, even before he checked anything?
qa.a: He felt panicky; his stomach flipped and his hands were already cold, just from the worry around him.

qa.q: Which choice did Vikas make on Friday, and why was it wise?
qa.a: When the sports day rumour started, he took a breath and went to ask at the staffroom, checking the facts before letting the worry spread through him.

qa.q: How might Mr Pillai have felt seeing the worried faces on Tuesday?
qa.a: Mr Pillai was probably puzzled and a little concerned that a rumour had frightened the whole class when nobody could say where it came from.

grounding: Shows a boy caught up in exam panic that spreads through his class faster than the facts, and later choosing to check before catching it.

subtype: Laughter and panic in a class [Actor]
passage: Ujjwal, you think only your class gets the giggles? Listen to your Parveen Nani. I was ten, in a small Aligarh school, and the inspector had come. Everyone sat straight like sticks. Then a lizard dropped from the ceiling onto the inspector's register. Shabnam in the front row made a tiny squeak. The girl behind her snorted. And then, beta, it went through the room like a wave. I didn't even see the lizard properly! But my shoulders were shaking, tears running, I couldn't stop. The teacher glared, which made it worse. The inspector finally laughed too, and said, 'Well, at least you're all awake.' Even now, when I remember it, I start smiling for no reason.

qa.q: What dropped onto the inspector's register?
qa.a: A lizard dropped from the ceiling onto the inspector's register.

qa.q: Why did Parveen Nani keep laughing even though she didn't see the lizard properly?
qa.a: She was caught up in the laughter spreading around her; the feeling moved through the room faster than knowing what had happened.

qa.q: What choice by the inspector helped the moment end well?
qa.a: The inspector laughed too and made a light joke instead of punishing anyone, which let the tension go.

qa.q: How might the teacher have felt while the class kept giggling in front of the inspector?
qa.a: The teacher was probably embarrassed and anxious about the inspection, and the glare only made the children laugh harder.

grounding: A grandmother tells her grandchild how, at ten, a giggle spread through her class during an inspection until she couldn't stop, without knowing what was funny.

subtype: Laughter and panic in a class [Actor]
passage: The power had gone out in the middle of the social science period, and Class 5 sat in the dim, hot room with the fans slowing to a stop. Suddenly there was a loud bang outside. A boy near the window shouted, 'Blast!' In a second, three children were under their desks and someone was screaming. Gurpreet hadn't heard anything but a bang. Still her heart was racing and she grabbed her bag and started crying. Nirmala ma'am stood very still at the front. 'Everyone look at me. Sit down. Breathe with me.' She sent the peon to check. He came back grinning: the school bus had a burst tyre. Gurpreet wiped her face, feeling a bit silly. Her heart kept thumping for a long time after.

qa.q: What did the boy near the window shout?
qa.a: He shouted, 'Blast!'

qa.q: Why did Gurpreet start crying when she had only heard a bang?
qa.a: She caught the fear from the shouting and screaming around her, so her heart raced even though she didn't know what had happened.

qa.q: What turning point calmed the class, and why did it work?
qa.a: Nirmala ma'am stood still, asked everyone to look at her and breathe, and sent someone to check, so her calm and then the facts replaced the panic.

qa.q: How might the boy near the window feel once he learned it was a burst tyre?
qa.a: He might feel embarrassed that his shout scared the whole class, and maybe relieved that nothing bad happened.

grounding: A girl is swept into a classroom panic during a power cut after one child shouts, showing fear spreading faster than facts.

subtype: Laughter and panic in a class [Actor]
passage: In the silent reading period at their Delhi school, the only sound was the ceiling fan. Then Ojas's stomach growled, long and low, like a creaky door. Sumit snorted. He clapped a hand over his mouth, but his shoulders shook. That set off the girl behind him, then the whole back row. Soon the class was wheezing, heads down on their books, and nobody even remembered why. Sumit's eyes streamed. Every time he tried to stop, he looked at Ojas, and it started again. Ma'am waited, then said, "Two minutes to laugh. Then books." They laughed harder, and then, slowly, it ran out.

qa.q: What sound set everything off?
qa.a: Ojas's stomach growled, long and low.

qa.q: Why couldn't Sumit stop laughing, even when he wanted to?
qa.a: He felt giddy and helpless to stop, as the laughter all around kept feeding his own and every look at Ojas started it again.

qa.q: Why did Ma'am's "two minutes to laugh" work better than scolding might have?
qa.a: It let the giggles run their course instead of fighting them, so they faded on their own and the class could go back to books 🙂

qa.q: How might Ojas have felt as the whole class laughed?
qa.a: Ojas may have felt embarrassed at first, but since nobody even remembered why they were laughing, it likely became shared fun rather than mockery.

grounding: A growling stomach sets off one snort that spreads through the whole class until nobody remembers why they are laughing.

subtype: Laughter and panic in a class [Actor]
passage:
"Payal! The science practical is tomorrow!"
"What? Who said?"
"Nirmala's cousin in 6B. Everyone's saying it."
"Tomorrow? I haven't even labelled my diagram!"
"Arre, Bunty is crying already."
"Nirmala, is it true?"
"I only said my cousin thought it might be early."
"But everyone's writing it down!"
"I know, I know. Now even I'm scared, and I started it."
"Should we ask Sir?"
"Yes. Come."
"Sir, is the practical tomorrow?"
"Tomorrow? No. Next Thursday, like the notice says."
"Oh."
"Then why is the whole class copying diagrams at lunch?"
"Sorry, Sir. It kind of... spread."

qa.q: When is the practical really?
qa.a: Next Thursday, like the notice says.

qa.q: How did Nirmala feel once the rumour had spread?
qa.a: Nirmala felt scared too, even after starting it, because everyone else's panic was catching.

qa.q: What choice stopped the panic, and why was it wise?
qa.a: Payal and Nirmala went to ask Sir directly, checking the fact instead of passing on the fear.

qa.q: What might the lunch break have been like for Bunty?
qa.a: Bunty was crying over a practical that wasn't happening, which shows the worry reached people long before any facts did.

grounding: A half-heard rumour about a practical spreads worry through a class faster than the facts, until two children check with the teacher.
